<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/driver-turso`, touching **15** documentable anchor(s).

**4** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/data-modeling/drivers.mdx`  _(via TursoDriver (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx`  _(via relax_not_null (symbol, a field of const object REMOTE_DRIFT_OP_ANSWERS), relax_not_null (literal, a string literal in applyRemoteColumnDriftOp))_
- `content/docs/plugins/packages.mdx`  _(via TursoDriver (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/protocol/objectql/query-syntax.mdx`  _(via TursoDriver (symbol, a top-level class))_

⛔ **2** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-5.mdx`  _(via TursoDriver (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-6.mdx`  _(via TursoDriver (symbol, a top-level class))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **8** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **8** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 9e6fee19ea358232196e1f704198612a2de34710` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `a54ba2467553f4bb6ab0301dae33dda9b7ae5275` — the merge of head `00fadc550bb6d2733fe43b0d2a5e1cce91ffbef8` into base `9e6fee19ea358232196e1f704198612a2de34710`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin a54ba2467553f4bb6ab0301dae33dda9b7ae5275 && git checkout a54ba2467553f4bb6ab0301dae33dda9b7ae5275
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 9e6fee19ea358232196e1f704198612a2de34710 00fadc550bb6d2733fe43b0d2a5e1cce91ffbef8 && git checkout -B drift-repro 9e6fee19ea358232196e1f704198612a2de34710 && git merge --no-ff 00fadc550bb6d2733fe43b0d2a5e1cce91ffbef8

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 9e6fee19ea358232196e1f704198612a2de34710
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 9e6fee19ea358232196e1f704198612a2de34710` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `a6797ba07c832692288d361978c8b162714a0d0f`
Local-runs: none

### ① Derived judgments

Read: card #33724 with all 16 comments (ruling 6915086281 letter A and its six parameters, claim 6915158382, amendment 6917885070, reports 6917853648 and 6919701288, cloud fact 6920763007), the PR body, the net diff of 12 files, the check-runs. No earlier contract-review record exists on this PR; 6919805011 is a decline, 6920860730 the claim.

- **`Clause-②: yes (widening)` is the right arm.** Nothing narrows. On the REMOTE face one drift op moves from always-skipped to applied; every other row of `REMOTE_DRIFT_OP_ANSWERS` is byte-identical, and the local face is not touched (`applyMigrationEntries` still returns `super` when not remote).
- **What newly widens, each named right by the PR:**
  - `TursoDriver.applyMigrationEntries` on REMOTE now sends DDL for `relax_not_null` and may answer it under `applied`. Right.
  - `TursoDriver.driftApplyLimit('relax_not_null')` on REMOTE answers `null` where it answered the rebuild sentence, so `os migrate plan` and the apply listing show the relax with no limit and the footer counts one fewer unappliable change. Right, pinned by the two CLI stub files.
  - The three doors (`relaxDeclaredNotNull`, `applyPublishedColumnChanges`, `os migrate apply`) stay `inherited` and reach the new arm; the publish no longer answers `object-column-changes-not-applied` for a relax that lands. Right (parameter 2). A remote schema sync still does not relax (pinned), so ADR-0113 D5 holds.
- **Named wrong, prose only:** the changeset and claim call `REMOTE_DRIFT_OP_ANSWERS` "exported". It is a module export of `turso-driver.ts`; `src/index.ts` does not re-export it and the package `exports` map has one entry, so no consumer can address it (0 uses outside driver-turso). The published widening is the behaviour of the two `TursoDriver` methods above. See N1.
- `remote-relax-not-null.ts` is not re-exported either: no new public symbol.
- **Ruling parameters against the code:** 1 relax only: holds. 3 applied only on a read-back of nullability, type, DEFAULT and pk: holds. 4 no fall-back: holds, every non-success path is `false`. 5 only nullability changes: holds, and more strictly than the ruling asked (the definition is cut from `sqlite_master.sql`, not rebuilt). 6 local face untouched: holds.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/driver-turso` patch, with `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: none` line-initial in both the PR body and the changeset. Correct: no metadata key or accepted value changes, and AGENTS.md ships a non-protocol widening as `patch`. Only driver-turso source moves; the runtime and CLI changes are tests, so no other package owes a changeset. `Check Changeset` is green.

### ③ Boundary flags

**Data safety of the in-place change (the code, read):**

- Atomic: the `ALTER` and its check go in one `write` batch (`RemoteTransport.batch`, one server transaction). The check compares the whole stored table SQL to the planned text and raises on any difference, so the outcome is either exactly "the NOT NULL clause removed, every other byte kept" or nothing. No row is copied, so there is no partial-copy state and no table can be left half-built. Re-running after any failure is safe: the arm re-reads the column first.
- No data-loss path found. The one loss the statement can cause (a CHECK, COLLATE, UNIQUE or REFERENCES clause dropped with the NOT NULL) is what the in-batch check exists to stop, and the PR's ablation shows the pragma read-back alone would miss it.
- Not resumable, and does not need to be: one statement, one transaction.
- No new id materialisation or in-app join.

**M1 (must-fix) — ruling parameter 4's first step is not met at this head.** The ruling makes pinning the statement against a real `sqld` the build's first step. `turso-remote-relax-not-null-sqld.test.ts` and the rewritten `apply.remote-face.integration.test.ts` cases are gated on `OS_TEST_SQLD_BIN`, CI has no `sqld`, and both reports say NOT MEASURED. Every measurement in the PR is on the embedded engine. Two things are therefore unknown on the server every hosted tenant runs: whether it accepts the statement, and whether its splice leaves the stored SQL byte-equal to the planned text. If it does not, the arm fails safe (rolled back, skipped) but the widening this PR declares does not exist on hosted. Required: run both gated files against a real `sqld`, record the result on the card; a refusal goes to the maintainer under parameter 4. No code change is implied by this finding.

**S1 (should-fix) — a measured refusal class has not been put to the maintainer.** The Acceptance note measures that libSQL refuses the relax for any column whose stored definition holds a comma (a DEFAULT, a CHECK, `NUMERIC(10, 2)`, a comment). Parameter 4 says a refusal comes back to the maintainer once; the 维护者速读 does not name it. Columns this face creates are `TYPE [NOT NULL]` (`remote-transport.ts` column renderer, read), so the card's own case is not in the class. For a column that is, `os migrate plan` lists the relax with no limit, every apply reports it not applied with exit 0, and no door on this transport clears it. Put that to him with M1's result, and say on the card what such a tenant does.

**N1 (nit)** — changeset wording "the exported `REMOTE_DRIFT_OP_ANSWERS`": not package-addressable (① above).

**N2 (nit)** — `applyRemoteRelaxNotNull`'s catch logs "the batch rolled back" for every thrown error. A transport error after the server committed has an unknown outcome; the entry is then reported skipped while the column is relaxed. The state is the wanted one and the next plan shows no drift, so only the log line is wrong.

**N3 (nit)** — the early `if (!before?.notNull) return false` logs nothing, while the CLI tells the operator "its log above says why".

**Docs line (`content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx`)**: matches the code sentence by sentence (in place, only the clause leaves, no row copied, applied only on the read-back, refusal leaves the column and lists the entry not applied, tightening and dropped DEFAULT keep the rebuild sentence). It omits the comma class the changeset names; fold into S1's outcome.

**Check-runs on the head:** 57 runs, none red, none running (success or skipped). The PR is draft.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `00fadc550bb6d2733fe43b0d2a5e1cce91ffbef8`
Local-runs: none

Delta round against this seat's FAIL 6920999561 (head `a6797ba0`), asked for by announce 6922371133. Read: the four delta commits (`6a05a50a`, `709476e3`, `715fc6a1`, `00fadc55`; 5 files, +95 −13), the card's six comments since that record (report 6921327686, measurement 6921391723 and addendum 6921439242, report 6921757949, ruling 6922037129, report 6922308957), the PR body, the check-runs. The merge-base with `main` is unchanged (`183a89e3`), so the delta is the whole change since the last record. The findings of 6920999561 that are not named below stand as written.

### ① Derived judgments

- **`Clause-②: yes (widening)` is still the right arm.** The delta publishes no new accept-set change. The only product hunk is the `catch` of `applyRemoteRelaxNotNull` and its two early returns: each still answers `false` (skipped), only the `warn` text differs. `REMOTE_DRIFT_OP_ANSWERS`, the batch, the in-batch check and the read-back are byte-identical to `a6797ba0`; `remote-relax-not-null.ts` and the sqld pin file are untouched.
- **No fall-back was added (ruling 6915086281 parameter 4, ruling 6922037129 item 1).** Read: the comma branch only appends a sentence to the log line and returns `skip(...)`. Right.
- **The log text now matches what happened.** A failed batch re-reads `sqlite_master.sql`: equal to the text read before the send is "nothing landed"; different or unreadable is "outcome unknown, the next drift read decides". The comma sentence is appended only on the "nothing landed" arm and only when the column's own stored definition holds a comma. Right, and each arm is pinned (comma case, comma-free refused case with a negative assertion, transport error after commit, converged re-run).
- **The changeset names the widening correctly now:** `TursoDriver.applyMigrationEntries` applies the entry and `TursoDriver.driftApplyLimit('relax_not_null')` answers `null` on the remote face. "Exported" is gone.

### ② Semver level

Unchanged and correct: `@objectstack/driver-turso` patch, `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: none` line-initial in the PR body and the changeset. The delta outside driver-turso is one docs paragraph and one test expectation, so no other package owes a changeset.

### ③ Boundary flags

**Earlier findings:**

- **M1 — closed.** The decision thread, not the building seat, measured the driver pin on official `sqld` 0.24.33 (image digest and binary sha256 recorded): 2/2 on `a6797ba0` (6921391723) and 2/2 on `709476e3` (6921439242). The server accepts the statement and the stored SQL is byte-equal to the planned text. The cli gated file was 8/9 in both, the one red reading `expected 'nothing_safe_to_apply' to be undefined`; `715fc6a1` changes exactly that expectation to `toBe('nothing_safe_to_apply')`, which is the value the independent run observed and the value `apply.ts` answers on that path (read). The 9/9 on `715fc6a1` and the 2/2 on this head are the building seat's own runs (6921757949, 6922308957); the product code they reach has not changed since the independent 2/2. Not re-run here.
- **S1 — closed by ruling 6922037129, letter A.** Its four items against the tree: the column keeps NOT NULL and no rebuild is added (holds); the apply lists the entry not applied and the reason names the class (holds, pinned, ablated per 6922308957); `cli.mdx` names the class and what the operator sees (holds, sentence by sentence against the code); platform-created columns are outside the class (holds: `mapFieldTypeToSQL` answers only `TEXT`, `INTEGER`, `REAL`, and `columnDeclarationSQL` adds only ` NOT NULL`). The 维护者速读 states the limit and cites the ruling.
- **N1, N2, N3 — closed** (changeset wording; the re-read before the log; both early returns log why, the already-nullable one pinned).

**New in this round. No must-fix, no should-fix.**

- **N4 (nit)** — `cli.mdx` and the changeset say platform-created columns have "no DEFAULT". `created_at` and `updated_at` are created as `TEXT DEFAULT (datetime('now'))`. Neither is NOT NULL and neither holds a comma, so the conclusion ("never in the class") is true; only the premise is too broad. "No declared-field DEFAULT" would be exact.
- **N5 (nit)** — the docs paragraph says what `os migrate apply` shows for a comma-class column, not that `os migrate plan` lists the same relax with no limit (the plan does not read the stored definition). Ruling 6922037129 left this wording to the seat and the reviewer; one clause would do.
- **N6 (nit)** — the PR body's `Acceptance notes` and `Verification` sections still read "not measured" for the real-`sqld` pin and the hosted splice; `Fix round 3` and `Fix round 4` lower in the same body supersede them.

**Open questions:** none in reports 6921327686, 6921757949, 6922308957. Still not measured, and named as such by the ruling: a hosted Turso database; that is the card's closing check, not this PR's.

**SQL push-down:** no new id materialisation or in-app join. The delta adds one catalog read on the failure path only.

**Check-runs on the head:** 57 runs, all concluded: 40 success, 17 skipped, none red, none running. The PR head is still this sha. The PR is draft.

## 席位核对 · ACCEPT (L1, first read) · Head-sha: 00fadc550bb6d2733fe43b0d2a5e1cce91ffbef8 · 2026-11-16T16:58Z

L1 thread L1-a for area o1-B, reading the final head declared in 6923107247. I read card #33724, maintainer rulings 6915086281 (letter A, six parameters) and 6922037129 (the comma class accepted), the PR body, review#2's PASS 6923055131 on this head, and the full diff against merge base `183a89e3`: 12 files, +914/−74. The PR is not governed, and the L2 is review#2's.

- **Card relation.** `Part of #33724`, which is right. This PR is the framework half. The cloud half is #34377, and the hosted-Turso measurement is the card's closing check, as review#2 also notes.
- **The six ruling parameters, against the code.**
  1. *Relax only.* `REMOTE_DRIFT_OP_ANSWERS.relax_not_null` becomes `'applied'`. `tighten_not_null`, the width entries and the dropped DEFAULT keep `needs-table-rebuild`. The comment says why: the statement does not revalidate rows.
  2. *Doors unchanged.* `relaxDeclaredNotNull` and `applyPublishedColumnChanges` stay `inherited` on this face, so the install or upgrade, the publish and `os migrate apply` reach it. No boot path changes (ADR-0113 D5).
  3. *Applied only on a read-back.* `applyRemoteRelaxNotNull` returns `true` only when `pragma_table_info` reads the column back nullable with the same `type`, `dflt_value` and `pk` as before. The stored-SQL check inside the batch covers every other clause.
  4. *A refusal is reported, with no fall-back.*
     - A planner refusal, a refused batch, or a read-back that differs returns `skip(reason)`. That logs a warning, and `applyMigrationEntries` reports the entry `skipped`. Nothing rebuilds.
     - A failed batch is called a rollback only when the stored SQL reads as before. Otherwise, or when it cannot be read, the log says the outcome is unknown.
     - The real-sqld pin (`turso-remote-relax-not-null-sqld.test.ts`, gated on `OS_TEST_SQLD_BIN`) passed 2/2 on official sqld 0.24.33 in the seat's measurement (6921391723 / 6921439242 on #33724).
  5. *Only nullability changes.*
     - `planRelaxedColumnDefinition` lexes the stored `CREATE TABLE`. Quotes in all four forms and both comment forms are single tokens, so commas and parentheses inside them never count.
     - It splits the column list at depth 1 and finds the one element named for the column, never a table-constraint opener. It cuts only `[CONSTRAINT name] NOT NULL [ON CONFLICT x]` at the definition's own depth, never inside a CHECK, a DEFAULT expression or a REFERENCES clause.
     - The result is checked inside the same `write` batch: the stored SQL must equal `expectedTableSql`, and a mismatch raises from a plain SELECT through `json()`. So a splice the plan did not predict rolls back. That is pinned (`a splice the plan did not predict lands nowhere`).
  6. *The local face keeps its rebuild.* The local arm is not touched.
- **The comma class (ruling 6922037129).** A definition holding a comma is refused by libSQL and the table is left byte-identical. This is pinned on the in-memory libSQL and measured on real sqld. The skip reason names the class ("holds a comma … keeps its NOT NULL"), no rebuild follows, and `cli.mdx` and the changeset name the class. All four of the ruling's terms are met.
- **Pins.**
  - `remote-relax-not-null.test.ts` (planner, 10 cases): every quoting form, a named constraint with ON CONFLICT, NOT DEFERRABLE and SET NULL inside REFERENCES not mistaken for the constraint, a table constraint never taken for the column, a string holding `NOT NULL`, the last column, and the refusals.
  - `turso-remote-migration-entries.test.ts` (5 new cases): applied with only the NOT NULL clauses leaving; the comma refusal with the table byte-identical; the unknown outcome; the check rolling the statement back; the declared `storage: { notNull: false }` path.
  - The cli, runtime and publish pins were re-pointed from "skipped, needs rebuild" to "applied", and `apply.remote-face.integration.test.ts` reads `nothing_safe_to_apply` once the relax has landed.
- **Changeset.** `patch` on `@objectstack/driver-turso` with `Clause-②: yes (widening)` (an entry that was skipped is now applied) and `Metadata-protocol: none`. Every bullet matches the code above.
- **Checks on this head** (check-runs): 61 names, 41 success, 19 skipped, 0 failed, 1 still running (`Check Changeset`) when I read them. Landing needs it green.
- **Base.** PRBASE is `9e6fee19` (Test Core plan), and K = 0.

### Notes (not blocking)

- review#2's N4 ("no DEFAULT" is too broad, since `created_at` and `updated_at` carry `DEFAULT (datetime('now'))`) and N5 (`os migrate plan` lists a comma-class relax with no limit) are left for a follow-up, per 6923107247. They are prose in `cli.mdx` and the changeset. Before landing, either name the card that carries them, or apply them on this branch as a prose-only move. The changeset sentence ships in the release notes once released, so fixing it before landing costs least.

Landing: not Tier H. Area o1-B lands it once `Check Changeset` is green.
